---
title: "Compilation, Coordinates, and Network Views"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING concept

This page explains the current candidate design. It does not define topology,
coordinate mathematics, execution, or failure behavior; the linked Runtime
Contract remains the sole authority.
:::

## Design pressure

One declared circuit often supports several analysis questions: an untouched
network response, a probe-compensated view, a paired-node representation, or a
smaller retained boundary. Copying or mutating the circuit for each question
would make it unclear which circuit produced an answer and would invite Direct
and HB to diverge.

## Selected abstraction {#network-view-lineage}

SCNSim keeps physical compilation with the original sealed Plan. A
`NetworkViewRef` is instead an immutable, ordered lineage from that Plan. Its
pipeline separates a change to the effective topology from a change to the
coordinates or boundary used to inspect it. Direct and HB consume the same
lineage, then either realize it faithfully or do not run it.

The final view names selected node coordinates, not a new circuit or a
backend-specific port list.

## Problem solved

This allows one model to support several honest views while retaining the
ancestry needed to explain each. It prevents a compensated probe from being
mistaken for a physical change, preserves coordinate identity through a
transform, and makes an omitted node a deliberate boundary choice rather than
a matrix slice with unstated assumptions.

## Intentionally not owned

This concept does not introduce a reduced `CircuitPlan`, manual transform
weights, a backend-specific reduction language, or public access to anonymous
internal coordinates. It also does not state the transform or elimination
mathematics; those normative definitions remain in the Runtime Contract and
its cited Knowledge pages.
